### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **89** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`
- **25** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **54** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `81faed8b9569db4470bcdff29fec07fb7006bcdc` — the merge of head `3100b841e32027af5f3d910cba6c6b70c4ca1b19` into base `1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 81faed8b9569db4470bcdff29fec07fb7006bcdc && git checkout 81faed8b9569db4470bcdff29fec07fb7006bcdc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404 3100b841e32027af5f3d910cba6c6b70c4ca1b19 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404 && git merge --no-ff 3100b841e32027af5f3d910cba6c6b70c4ca1b19

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1aeeafd9d371be1fd5afa637c4f0ae6b6f4c1404` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3100b841e32027af5f3d910cba6c6b70c4ca1b19`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/package-upgrade-plan.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-upgrade-environment.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/diff.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts, .changeset/30884-package-upgrade-plan.md + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts, packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/local-manifest-source.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/cli/tsconfig.test.json

PR 1 of card #30884, the widening half. The Q3 refusal is PR 2 and is not judged here. Head `3100b841` is still the PR head. Base `616311c1`, merge base the same; main is 17 commits ahead and none of those commits touches any of the 13 changed files (measured with `git diff --name-only` over those paths: empty).

### ① Derived judgments

**Must-fix: none.**

**Should-fix (does not block this PR):**

- S1. `packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts:374`, `:457-465`. `--dry-run` sends `dryRun: true` and nothing else. A runtime that predates the key reads the body as before (`body: any`, no closed key set, see ② below) and installs. The command detects this only from the answer and exits 1 after the install has happened. The PR body and the handoff both say so. The flag's own sentence is "installs nothing", and against any runtime from before this release that sentence is false. No pre-send probe exists in `install.ts` (only the auth call at `:341`). Recommend a card: a pre-send probe of the runtime (or a refusal to send `dryRun` to a runtime whose answer shape cannot be known), so the flag can never install.
- S2. `packages/objectql/src/package-upgrade-environment.ts:317`. `isOverwrittenEdit` skips a column the installed seed did not write (`if (!(column in installed)) continue;`). A customer value in a column the installed seed left unset, which the incoming seed now writes, is a customer edit the replay erases, and it is not counted. This under-reports, never over-reports. The card's acceptance case (one edited row of three) passes because the edit is in a column both seeds write. Recommend counting that case too: when `installed` lacks the column, treat the seeded value as absent and count the row when the stored value is non-null and differs from the incoming value.

**Confirmed, by file and line:**

Gate 1, dryRun writes nothing.
- `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1784` runs `requireInstallCapability` first, before the body is read (`:1790`). `:1815-1842` is step 0′: `dryRun` must be absent or a boolean, else `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; `dryRun` with `installMode: 'unmanaged'` is `400`. `:2272-2286` refuses a dry run of a customization pair. `:2382-2389` is step 2a′: `if (dryRun) return this.answerUpgradeDryRun(...)`, after the conflict check (2) and the held-datasource check (2a), before the D5e ceremony (2b), the access gate (2c) and the first write (3).
- Between step 0′ and 2a′ every operation is a read: the cloud fetch (`:1891-1940`), payload parse, id parse (1b), handshake (1c), install-mode judgment (1e), `unrunnableCode` (1d, `:2199`), `judgeWithheldMaps` (1d′, `:2215`), the conflict check (2), `findHeldDatasourceName` (2a). The `unmanaged` branch (`:2227`) and the pair branch (`:2272`) both write, and both are refused for a dry run before they run.
- `answerUpgradeDryRun` (`:4919-4961`) reads the ledger (`LocalManifestSource.read`, `local-manifest-source.ts:398-407`: `existsSync` + `readFileSync`, no write), converts both bodies forward and calls `planUpgrade`. `convertPackageBodyForward` (`engine.ts`, `engine-package-registration.ts`) is a pure conversion with one in-memory "already warned" memo for its log line; no file, registry, seed, metadata, activation-ledger, audit or cache write. A `manifest` service with no `planUpgrade` answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, never an empty plan (`:4926-4935`).
- Body key validation: the body is `any` from `readJsonRequestBody` (`:1790-1792`). There is no closed key set on this route and never was: an unknown key is ignored, not refused, before and after this PR. `dryRun` is validated by its own `typeof` check at `:1823`. The only key whose handling changed is `dryRun` itself: a non-boolean `dryRun`, ignored before, is now `400`.
- `dryRun` with other keys: with `confirmAccessUpgrade`, the token is ignored because the dry run answers at 2a′, before the access gate at 2c (the PR says so). With `packageId`, the manifest is fetched from the cloud and then planned. With `installMode: 'managed'` or absent, the plan runs; with `'unmanaged'`, `400`. With `manifest` inline, the plan runs against the inline body.
- Test `marketplace-install-local-upgrade-plan.test.ts:127-152` pins `register` and `syncSchemas` never called and the ledger directory byte for byte; `:166-173` is the control (the same body without `dryRun` installs and `planUpgrade` is not called); `:175-184` the 503; `:188-205` the two 400s.

Gate 2, the comparison against Expected 1.
- Added and removed objects: `package-upgrade-plan.ts:316-317`. Added and removed fields with `required` and `stored`: `:340-351`, `describeField` at `:181`.
- Type changes carry a category: `:366-372`, `typeChangeCategory` at `:202-208`. The category is derived from the storage fact (`isVirtualSearchField`, `search-fields.ts:159`), not from a live column: installed field computed → `safe`; new field computed → `destructive` (the driver's `drop_column` op is destructive, `schema-drift.ts:464`); both stored → `needs_confirm` (the driver's `manual_column_type_change` is `needs_confirm`, `schema-drift.ts:1257-1258`, and the comment at `:1141-1157` says the gate reads category only). A pure function cannot see the physical column, so a retype the live driver would call `destructive` (narrowing) is `needs_confirm` here. PR 2 decides what confirms; both words are above `safe`.
- Declared renames via `renamedFrom`: `:329-338`. A new key whose `renamedFrom` names an installed key the new version no longer declares. The source is not listed as removed (`:342`) and the target not as added (`:348`). The first matching `renamedFrom` entry wins; `refuseDishonestRenamedFrom` in spec already refuses an old key two fields claim.
- A declared rename whose type changes is ALSO a type change, at any category: `:353-373`. The type-change test at `:366` is `from !== to` with no category condition, and `target !== key` only adds `renamedFrom` to the finding. Test `package-upgrade-plan.test.ts:78-92` pins the `needs_confirm` case (text → number on a declared rename), which is exactly the case scope note 6685166393 names. The scope note holds.
- Suspected renames: `:375-389`. Within one object, each removed stored field with every unlinked added stored field as a candidate. Computed fields on either side are not candidates (they have no column); the card's sentence does not say "stored", but a computed field is no rename hazard, so this is a faithful reading. Both keys stay listed as removed and added.
- Seed datasets with their mode: `compareSeeds` at `:273-294`; the default mode comes from `SeedSchema.shape.mode.parse(undefined)` at `:212` (spec default `ignore`), not a copy. Changed means records, mode, columns or env. Test `:149-194`.
- Type-equality pin: `packages/cli/test/diff-upgrade-plan.test.ts:26-27`, `Equal<UpgradeDriftCategory, DriftCategory>` assigned `true`. It is real: `packages/cli/tsconfig.test.json:179-184` includes `test/**/*`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit && pnpm check:test-typecheck` (`packages/cli/package.json:31`), and the check-run "Type Check · debt ledger" is green on this head. A word added to or dropped from either union makes this line a new error outside the debt ledger. The runtime `expect(driftWordsAgree).toBe(true)` at `:65` is decoration; the pin is the `tsc` line.

Gate 3, `os diff` unchanged.
- On `main` there is no output fixture for `os diff` (`packages/cli/test/`: `commands.test.ts` and `normalized-call-sites.test.ts` reference the command's registration, `diff-usage-error-stream.e2e.test.ts` its usage error). Commit `60c95956d0` adds `diff-upgrade-plan.test.ts` with a byte-for-byte pin (`JSON.stringify`, entry and key order) over removed/added objects, required/optional field additions, field removal, type change, label change and every name-level category, and lifts the comparison into `diffStacks` unchanged. Commit `3714e769bd` moves `diffStacks` onto the plan. `git diff 60c95956d0 3714e769bd -- packages/cli/test/diff-upgrade-plan.test.ts` shows only an appended second `describe`; the pinned block (`:62-93`) did not move. No expectation was rewritten.
- Read against the old code: entry shapes and order are the same (`diff.ts:88-134` on the head, `:89-158` on the base). `getNames` (`:34-41`) and the plan's `objectsByName` both take the last declaration of a name. Type detection is the same (`oldType && newType && oldType !== newType` versus `typeOf` requiring a non-empty string).
- Two output changes exist and are stated in the PR body and changeset, not silent: a `renamedFrom` pair prints one `modified` entry instead of a removal plus an addition; a stored field removed beside a stored field added in one object prints an extra `modified` entry (`suspected rename to …`), and seed datasets print under `data` last. The pinned fixture holds neither pattern, so "unchanged for its existing fixtures" is true of the fixtures and the PR says what is new.

Gate 4, the environment half.
- Read-only: `package-upgrade-environment.ts:195-196` (`engine.count` with `$ne: null`), `:155` (`engine.count` per removed object), `:365-366` (`engine.find` with `$in` over the first match-key column). No write call in the module. `find` carries no default `limit` (`engine-find.ts:312`), so every matched row is read; the read is bounded by the dataset's own key values.
- Scoping: every read passes `{ context: { isSystem: true } }` (`:122`), with no organization. The counts are environment-wide across every organization, on purpose (`:28-29`): a package install here is environment-wide, one ledger per environment, and the caller is gated by `manage_metadata` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:399`), an environment operator. So yes, a dry run counts every organization's rows, and that is what the install would touch. The method takes no organization argument; see ③ for the hosted door.
- A failed reading is `null`: `reading()` at `:160-170` returns `null` and calls `warn` once with the object and the error. `rows` starts `null` (`:180`); `matchedRows` and `editedRows` start `null` (`:344`) and are set only after a successful `find` (`:386-387`). Test `:127-135` pins `null` and the warning.
- No cell values in the plan: the answer carries counts and, per overwriting dataset, up to 20 `editedKeys` (`:383`). A key is the natural key of a row that matched an incoming seed record (`:375-376`), so its text equals a key the package itself ships. No other row value leaves the function.
- Edited-row comparison: `isOverwrittenEdit` at `:313-327`. A row counts when some column the replay writes holds a value that is neither the installed seed's value nor the incoming one, in storage form (`blankStorageForm`, `temporalStorageForm`), skipping `id`, the match key, `applyOn: 'create'` columns, computed, masked, file and reference columns, and expression values. A row the installed version did not seed is matched but not counted (`:380`). Correct for the card's case (test `:76-96`: three seeded rows, the relabelled `lost` is an upgrade, the edited `won` counts). The one gap is S2 above.
- `planUpgrade` wiring: `plugin.ts:1039-1043` passes `ql`, `ql.registry.getObject` and `ctx.logger.warn`. Test `:183-204` runs it through a kernel with a multi-package artifact.

Gate 5, who may call.
- `requireInstallCapability` (`:1784`) runs before the body is parsed, so before `dryRun` is read: anonymous → 401, a held session → 403, no `manage_metadata` → `403 FORBIDDEN` (`:5954-5977`). The dry run has exactly the install's gate. The counts are disclosed only to a principal who could install, and they are environment-wide aggregates, not another tenant's rows. The dry run does not run the D5e ceremony (2b) or the access gate (2c), so a dry run can say "plan" for an install the real call would then refuse; the PR states this. That ordering discloses nothing beyond the plan.

Gate 7, tests and ablations, read not run.
- Suspected-rename ablation (`storedAdded` forced empty): `package-upgrade-plan.test.ts:53` (one suspected rename), `:93` (the unlinked `renamedFrom` case expects a suspected rename), `:111` (two candidates) go red; the rest hold. 3/17, as reported.
- Declared-rename type ablation (type change limited to `target === key`): `:78` goes red; nothing else asserts a type change on a renamed key. 1/17, as reported.
- Dry-run guard ablation (step 2a′ removed): `marketplace-install-local-upgrade-plan.test.ts:127` (`register` called, ledger moves), `:154` (ledger entry appears), `:175` (installs instead of 503) go red; the control, the non-boolean and the unmanaged cases still pass because step 0′ stays. 3/6, as reported.
- Every card acceptance bullet this PR carries has a named test, and I found each one in the file at the line the PR names.

Gate 8, check-runs on `3100b841`, latest run per name: 23 green (among them Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI); 10 in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace); 13 skipped (UI, docs, opt-in harnesses); none red. `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: blocked`: the lag of 17 commits is not a conflict (no overlap on any changed file); `blocked` is the pending required checks and the review this record supplies. Landing waits for the ten to finish green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30884-package-upgrade-plan.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/cli`. Correct by AGENTS.md's rule: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. New exports from `metadata-core` (`index.ts:164`), a new `planUpgrade` method on the `manifest` service, a new `dryRun` body key, a new `--dry-run` flag, new `os diff` entries. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two declaration lines. "Nothing a request did before answers differently" holds with one hairline: a non-boolean `dryRun`, ignored before, is now `400`. No client sent that key, so this is not a narrowing anyone can meet.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The PR reads `renamedFrom` (landed with #30934) and adds nothing an author can write.
- The install-local body is not declared in `packages/spec`. `packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts:391-403` declares the import body of the unmanaged import door, not this route; `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` reads `body: any` with per-key checks in the handler. `dryRun` is accepted by its own `typeof` check (`:1823`). No spec file is owed. The two codes the dry run answers (`INVALID_REQUEST`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) are standard catalog codes this plugin already uses; no ledger hunk is owed in PR 1.
- Served tier: the recogniser (`record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths <13 paths>`) finds no published-schema or governed path and maps the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line to the declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`. contract-review.md says a `Clause-②: yes`-only diff owes `TIER_DEFAULT` and the tier is exact, not a floor, so this record is served at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The review itself was run at the depth the claim (6686492425) asked for; the judgments do not change with the tier.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's `open_questions` are all PR 2 (ledger code name, the declared-rename refusal shape, what the verdict reads, where the gate sits). None bears on PR 1. On the third, the dev's option A (verdict from the pure comparison, readings attached when `planUpgrade` exists) is consistent with this PR's 503 for a dry run without `planUpgrade`: a preview that cannot run is refused, a verdict must not hinge on a reading. Carry that distinction into PR 2.
- The older-runtime hazard (S1) is a CLI contract flag for the seat: file a card, or fold a pre-send probe into PR 2.
- `planUpgrade(installed, incoming)` takes no organization and reads with the system context across every organization. Cloud's hosted install door (sibling card 01c, `repo:cloud`) must call it per environment, never per organization within a shared runtime, or it will show one organization another's counts. Name this in 01c's claim.
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` has no row for `--dry-run`; outside this claim's file surface, noted by the dev, not filed. The seat cards it.
- The dry run emits the forward-conversion warning for the incoming body once and marks it warned in memory, so a real install in the same process will not print it a second time. Benign; stated so the log is not read as a missing conversion.
- PR author `user.login` is `os-elon-musk`, not `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: the PR was created off-relay by the seat's account (dev report, `api_writes`). Read before landing, as the review rules ask.
- Head `3100b841` is unchanged from the dev report and the handoff. Local verification in the PR body (gates, suites, typecheck) was not re-run here; the check-runs are the measure.

### ④ Design judgment

- The comparison's home (`metadata-core`, a package `cli`, `objectql` and `cloud-connection` already depend on, so no new edge) holds against the card: one function, read by `os diff`, the door and the service. The three drift words are restated and pinned by type to the driver's, which is the right shape for a package that cannot depend on a driver.
- The scope note is honoured in the code, not only in a test: the type-change rule reads no category and no rename.
- Step 2a′ is placed where the card asks: after every refusal that says the package cannot install, before any ceremony and before the first write. Answering before the ceremonies is the right trade for a preview; the PR says what it does not say.
- The environment half restates the seed loader's private `seedValueEquals` through the same `@objectstack/core` functions. Two homes for one comparison is a drift risk; the dev noted the follow-up. Not blocking.
- S1 is the one place where the shipped sentence ("installs nothing") can be false. It is disclosed and reversible, and the fix sits on the CLI side; it does not block this PR.
